source_text: Accipiens Petrum et duos filios Zebedaei coepit tristari et taediari. Hos ipsos discipulos assumpsit et in monte cum transfigurandus esset. Coepit tristari — multum interest inter tristari et incipere tristari. Tentatus per omnia secundum similitudinem praeter peccatum, non tristatus est tristitia passionis ipsius sed secundum humanam naturam coepit.
pass_a_gloss: Taking Peter and two sons of Zebedee he-began to-be-sorrowful and to-be-wearied. These-same disciples he-took-along and on mountain when he-was-to-be-transfigured. He-began to-be-sorrowful — much it-differs between to-be-sorrowful and to-begin to-be-sorrowful. Tempted through all things according-to likeness apart-from sin, not sorrowed-was with sadness of passion itself but according-to human nature he-began.
pass_b_english: Taking [[Peter and the two sons of Zebedee >> Bible:Matthew 26:37]], he [[began to be sorrowful and troubled >> Bible:Matthew 26:37]]. These same disciples he had taken onto the mountain when he was to be transfigured. He began to be sorrowful — there is a great difference between being sorrowful and beginning to be sorrowful. [[Tempted in every way as we are, yet without sin >> Bible:Hebrews 4:15]], he was not simply swallowed by the passion’s sadness but, according to human nature, began.
notes: Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
